sources.shortCitation: NAC 3/1/0/6/2661/7 — guests at the young lawyers’ ball in Warsaw, with Emanuel Schlechter
sources.fullCitation: Narodowe Archiwum Cyfrowe, Koncern Ilustrowany Kurier Codzienny – Archiwum Ilustracji, sygn. 3/1/0/6/2661/7 (dawna sygn. 1-P-2661-7): „Grupa uczestników balu. Widoczni od lewej: reżyser Józef Lejtes (2. z lewej), malarka Gena Galewska, autor tekstów piosenek Emanuel Schlechter (występuje również jako Szlechter) i producent filmowy Norbert Tarler.” Unit „Bal młodych prawników w Warszawie”, 1930–1939. Photographer unidentified.
sources.title: Bal młodych prawników w Warszawie — group of ball guests with Emanuel Schlechter
sources.creator: Photographer unidentified
sources.researchNote: The catalogue gives the date range 1930–1939, not an exact year, and records the rights as expired (“Wygasły”); no author or photographic studio is named. The object caption identifies the sitters from the left, which places Schlechter fourth from the left, between Gena Galewska and Norbert Tarler.

media.title: Emanuel Schlechter — detail of a group photograph at a Warsaw ball, 1930s
media.description: Identification follows the archival caption, which names the guests from the left: the director Józef Lejtes second from the left, the painter Gena Galewska, the lyricist Emanuel Schlechter (also spelled Szlechter) and the film producer Norbert Tarler. Schlechter is the fourth figure from the left, in round spectacles, between Galewska and Tarler. The detail is an unretouched 640 × 810 px crop from the 3500 × 2768 px scan.
media.altText: Young man in round spectacles, evening dress with a white bow tie and a rosette on the lapel, smiling slightly.
media.rightsNote: Public domain. The frame is a Polish press photograph of the 1930s from the Koncern Ilustrowany Kurier Codzienny archive, with no photographer named and without the reservation of copyright that Polish law required before a photograph was protected. It was therefore already in the public domain in Poland on 1 January 1996, the United States restoration date, so the URAA restored nothing. Narodowe Archiwum Cyfrowe records the rights in the object as expired (“Wygasły”). The displayed 640 × 810 px detail is cropped from the 3500 × 2768 px scan of the group photograph.
media.publicCaption: Emanuel Schlechter, author of the Polish words to Kaper’s “San Francisco”, at the young lawyers’ ball in Warsaw in the 1930s. Detail of a group photograph with Józef Lejtes, Gena Galewska and Norbert Tarler.
